shortDescription: Shares of EVgo NASDAQ:EVGO opened about 3% lower on Tuesday after it trimmed its full-year 2026 outlook after third-quarter revenue fell short of expectations, despite growth in its core charging business.Third-quarter revenue fell 1% year over year to $91.42 million, missing consensus estimates by…

children: opened about 3% lower on Tuesday after it trimmed its full-year 2026 outlook after third-quarter revenue fell short of expectations, despite growth in its core charging business.

Third-quarter revenue fell 1% year over year to $91.42 million, missing consensus estimates by $3.2 million. The company reported a GAAP loss of 14 cents per share, compared with a loss of 9 cents a year earlier.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $3.5 million from $5 million a year earlier, beating the consensus estimate of a $6 million loss.

Charging network revenue rose 29% to $71.8 million, marking the 19th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Network throughput increased 8% to 103 gigawatt-hours, while charging network gross margin expanded 380 basis points to 39%.

lowered its 2026 revenue outlook to a midpoint of $387.5 million from $415 million previously. Its adjusted EBITDA forecast was revised to a midpoint loss of $22.5 million, compared with a midpoint profit of $15 million previously. The company also reduced its target for new stall additions to a midpoint of 1,175, down from 1,487.5 previously.

RBC downgraded the stock to 'sector perform' from 'outperform,' citing the lower guidance and throughput that fell short of expectations. The brokerage said macroeconomic conditions were weighing on deployment, although early demand indicators for its North American Charging Standard network were encouraging. The brokerage raised its price target to $2 from $1.75, reflecting the proposed take-private offer.
While UBS maintained a 'neutral' rating and a $2 price target, saying growth and margin improvement in EVgo’s

charging network were encouraging, but the reduced outlook pointed to a more mixed near-term picture. Its valuation also reflects the proposed offer, with risks if the transaction fails or cash burn remains elevated.
was taking “a disciplined approach to capital allocation,” prioritizing higher-return sites, network utilization, and cost efficiencies.
Shares have fallen about 37.5% so far this year, compared to the 10.3% rise in the broader index.
Short interest on EVGO stands at 24.24% of the total float.

title: EVgo posts mixed Q3 results, lowers 2026 guidance
